news.title: Meta ships Muse Voice Transcribe for live speech
news.body: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Voice Transcribe, a real-time speech transcription model with speaker diarization and adaptive delay. It is available now in Meta AI and through the Meta Model API at $0.18 per hour.
news.why: Developers and Meta AI users can buy live transcription with speaker labels at a listed API price today.
news.notes: Scout filed 4 items (under 10); thin run so this is not a full choice set.

news.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft
news.body: The Seattle Times and Newsday filed a copyright lawsuit in the Southern District of New York against OpenAI and Microsoft. The suit alleges scraping of paywalled journalism for AI training and related claims.
news.why: Two more newsrooms are seeking court limits on how OpenAI and Microsoft use paywalled reporting in training and products.

news.title: Authors contest claims on Anthropic settlement payouts
news.body: Authors in Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement say publishers and some literary agents are filing claim shares that conflict with the settlement's 50-50 split or rights-reversion rules. The settlement pays about $3,000 per pirated work under those allocation rules.
news.why: Authors deciding whether to dispute payment allocations face conflicting claims that can cut what they receive from the settlement.
news.notes: only one link filed by the Scout

coding.name: Coding projects
coding.why: Claude Fable 5.1 leads Terminal-Bench v2.1 and SciCode outright. GPT-5.6 Sol is 3 points back.
coding.tests: Terminal-Bench hands the model a command line and a real job (install this, fix that build, process these files) and checks whether it finishes. SciCode has it write working code for research problems.
coding.daily: "Can it do technical chores on a computer by itself, and is the code it writes correct?"

agents.name: Supervising coding agents
agents.why: Claude Fable 5.1 leads GDPval-AA v2 and Terminal-Bench v2.1 outright. Claude Opus 5 is 2 points back, within noise.
agents.tests: Blends the long, multi-step tests: real job deliverables judged against other models (GDPval), following rules while using tools across a long conversation (τ³-Banking), terminal work, and reasoning over long documents.
agents.daily: "When I hand it a big project and walk away, will it keep track, follow instructions, and not go off the rails?"

frontend.name: Frontend and design
frontend.why: GPT-6 Astra leads Arena WebDev outright. Claude Fable 5.1 is 4 points back.
frontend.tests: Arena WebDev shows two models the same request, builds both sites, and asks people which they prefer. Terminal-Bench adds whether it can actually ship the code.
frontend.daily: "Which one makes the page people like more, and can it build it?" Mostly a taste vote.

image.name: Image generation
rows: Nano Banana 2 Lite (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image)
image.why: GPT Image 2 is ranked 3 of 159 on this board at 1171. The board leader is GPT Image 2.5 Flare (max) at 1187, which you cannot open.
image.tests: Blind human votes between two images made from the same prompt.
image.daily: "Which image tool do people prefer?" Pure preference, no task test exists.

video.name: Video generation
video.why: Grok Imagine Video is ranked 10 of 83 on this board at 1225. The board leader is Wan 3.0 at 1334, which you cannot open.
video.tests: Blind human votes between two clips made from the same prompt, across the whole video board rather than the audio-only chart.
video.daily: "Which video tool do people prefer?" Pure preference. Sora is not on this board at all.

writing.name: Writing to humans
writing.why: GPT-6 Astra has the best blend across the tests without leading any one of them. Grok 4.6 is 0 points back, within noise.
writing.tests: Arena Text is a blind vote on which reply people prefer in ordinary chat. Non-hallucination is how often the model admits it does not know instead of bluffing. Accuracy is plain factual recall.
writing.daily: "Which one writes the way people like, and will it quietly make things up in my email?"

audit.name: Auditing code
audit.why: Grok 4.6 has the best blend across the tests without leading any one of them. GPT-6 Astra is 6 points back.
audit.tests: Coding tests plus the bluffing rate, because a reviewer that invents bugs is worse than none.
audit.daily: "Will it find the real problems in this code without inventing fake ones?"

technical.name: Technical jobs
technical.why: Claude Fable 5.1 leads Terminal-Bench v2.1 and GDPval-AA v2 outright. Claude Opus 5 is 2 points back, within noise.
technical.tests: Terminal work, real job deliverables, and long-document reasoning.
technical.daily: "Data cleanup, scripts, configuring things, reading a long spec: can it handle the whole job?"
